section_summary: This section continues a Japanese economic rehabilitation report covering planned trade, national income, production, investment, public finance, employment, and living standards through 1953. It ends with a discussion of the balance of payments, terms of trade, and Japan’s dependence on economic recovery in East Asia. The final two pages repeat part of the same discussion.

subfiles.title: Economic Rehabilitation Program
subfiles.about: A five-year program projects how Japan could restore production, expand exports, finance investment, and reach an internationally sustainable economy.
subfiles.summary: This portion of the report sets targets for imports, exports, national income, industrial and agricultural output, transport, housing, public finance, employment, and consumption through 1953. It gives detailed investment programs for electric power, shipping, manufacturing, agriculture, and disaster prevention, alongside proposals for technical research and training. The closing discussion argues that a viable balance of payments depends on limiting essential imports, earning shipping revenue, improving the terms of trade, and restoring markets in East Asia.
